results.title: Partial Identification in Applied Research
results.content: However it is still possible to learn about such quantities even if they are not.1 Econometric models that allow for partial identiﬁcation, or partially identifying models, make fewer assumptions and use them to generate bounds on the parameters of interest. Ho, Ho, and Mortimer (2012) and Lee (2013) both use moment inequalities as a means to estimate bounds 14 on ﬁrm ﬁxed costs, as an input to modeling product choices in a particular industry, without making the assumptions needed to ensure point identiﬁcation of supply. Chesher and Rosen (2014) study partial identiﬁcation in structural econometric models, and focus their analysis on obtaining sharp bounds on structural functions and distributions of unobserved heterogeneity by using properties of the set of possible values of unobservables that may occur given observed variables. They show how to use partial identiﬁcation to estimate bounds on the parameters of these models semi-parametrically, without imposing commonly-used restrictions on the joint distribution of the unobservables across choices or their correlations across time or within groups.
